messages:
Mia (support): reporting from customer call — AcmeFin sees intermittent 300-600ms spikes and a bunch of requests routing to EU region even though they pinned to us-west. Customer says latency and billing are both impacted. request id examples: req_47a3, req_47b8.
infra-bot: New ticket created: #SUP-4987 (automated) — attached logs requested.
Tom (AcmeFin): Confirming — production traffic started hitting eu-west endpoints around 03:10 UTC. Our app is in us-west-2 VPC with a private NAT stack + peering to partner hub. No config changes on our side. :frowning:
Mia (support): Thanks Tom. Can you run one quick curl from an affected host and paste headers? e.g. curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACT' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/complete
Tom (AcmeFin): Paste: HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 03:12:07 GMT
X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1
X-Request-Id: req_47a3
Content-Type: application/json

(body)...
Mia (support): That X-Redwood-Region header is the smoking gun. It shows the request terminated in EU. Asking eng-net to jump in.
Raj (eng-net): looking. Quick questions: which egress IP are you SNATing to? can you tcpdump on the host and share 1s of packets to api.redwood.ai? Also share your route table for the VPC and any peered hub route table.
Tom (AcmeFin): SNAT IP shown in our gateway: 18.197.45.21. I'll run tcpdump now and traceroute.
Tom (AcmeFin): tcpdump (filter host api.redwood.ai) output snippet:
10:12:06.123456 IP 10.0.5.14.41234 > 3.227.12.45.443: Flags [S], seq 12345...
10:12:06.223456 IP 10.0.5.14.41234 > 52.19.45.99.443: Flags [S], seq 23456...
(note: 3.227.12.45 and 52.19.45.99 resolve to eu-west cluster IPs in our DNS)
Selene (sre): interesting — DNS may be returning multiple A records across regions, and the SNAT path chooses an egress that results in EU peering. Does your hub have asymmetric NAT/policy routing? If SNAT chooses partner egress in eu region, that would explain it.
Raj (eng-net): please paste your VPC route table and the NAT gateway config. Also, can you run curl with --resolve to force us-west domain to verify path? Example: curl -i --resolve api.redwood.ai:443:18.197.245.67 https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACT'
Tom (AcmeFin): Route table: 10.0.0.0/16 -> local; 0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-0a1b2c3d (this nat is an onprem peering tunnel). NAT config: primary SNAT pool ranges to partner hub, and fallback uses provider egress which is in eu.
Tom (AcmeFin): curl --resolve shows when forced to a us-west IP we get ~30ms. Default DNS results in round-robin including eu IPs and our NAT chosen path hits eu egress.
Mia (support): So DNS + SNAT egress preference + peering hub = wrong-region termination. Escalating to eng-net for mitigation and to SRE for transient fallback policy.
Raj (eng-net): root cause hypothesis: the peering hub advertises more-specific route to the internet via partner (which uses eu egress), and connection tracking preserves src->snat mapping so subsequent requests end up via eu. Fix options: 1) adjust SNAT to use region-local public IPs (policy-based SNAT), 2) update hub to avoid advertising that next-hop for destination ranges, 3) set DNS affinity by using region-pref A record order + EDNS client subnet, or 4) configure our API to honor X-Region header to prefer local nodes.
Selene (sre): short-term mitigation: we can add a routing rule on the NAT host to use ip rule/ip route table lookup based on destination to prefer gateway with us-west egress for api.redwood.ai. Example (on linux):
ip rule add to 18.0.0.0/8 lookup uswest_table pref 100
ip route add default via 18.197.245.1 dev eth0 table uswest_table
Also remove SNAT for traffic matching 52.19.0.0/16 and 3.0.0.0/8 (our infra ranges) so source IP preserves and provider routes correctly.
Raj (eng-net): I agree. We'll also add a ConnMark-based rule in iptables to mark traffic to api.redwood.ai and force route selection so connection tracking doesn't flip to partner egress mid-flow. Sample iptables:
iptables -t mangle -A OUTPUT -p tcp -d 3.227.0.0/16 -j CONNMARK --set-mark 0x1
ip rule add fwmark 0x1 lookup uswest_table

Mia (support): Noted. Tom, do you want us to push a temporary route change or do you want to apply on your side? We can remote in with you.
Tom (AcmeFin): Please push it — need this off ASAP. We've seen a 3x billing delta when traffic exits eu due to egress charges and increased latencies in UX.
Selene (sre): We'll schedule a quick maintenance: apply policy SNAT + ip rule tonight at 03:50 UTC, monitor for 15m, roll back if issues. I'll prepare rollback steps.
Raj (eng-net): I'll coordinate the hub team to stop advertising the partner next-hop for the specific public ranges. Also will open a follow-up to standardize per-service egress policies to prevent recurrence.
Mia (support): I'll update ticket #SUP-4987 with repro, mitigation plan, and ETA. Communicating to AcmeFin ops now.
Tom (AcmeFin): Appreciate the fast turnaround. Please send confirmation when done.
infra-bot: Action recorded: SUP-4987 updated — mitigation scheduled 2026-03-18T03:50:00Z.
Mia (support): closing loop: after change we validated headers — X-Redwood-Region: us-west-2 on subsequent requests and latency dropped back to baseline. Customer confirmed billing lookahead improved. Marking resolved after 24h observation. :white_check_mark:
